messages.author: 3a775dfa0a96bf95
messages.subject: Parameterizing column in aes
parts:
I can parameterize what variable I want to plot in ggplot by constructing my own 'aes' object, like this:

data <- data.frame(a=1:10,b=11:20)
col <- quote(b)   # parameter to below
ggplot(data) + geom_point( structure(list(x=quote(a), y= col ), class= "uneval"))

or
aese <- function(...) structure(eval(substitute(list(...))), class="uneval")
ggplot(data) + geom_point( aese(x=quote(a), y= col ))

Is there a cleaner or more standard way to do this?

            -s

>
> data<- data.frame(a=1:10,b=11:20)
> col<- quote(b) # parameter to below
> ggplot(data) + geom_point( structure(list(x=quote(a), y= col ), class=
> "uneval"))
>
> or
>
> aese<- function(...) structure(eval(substitute(list(...))), class="uneval")
> ggplot(data) + geom_point( aese(x=quote(a), y= col ))
>
>
> Is there a cleaner or more standard way to do this?

There is aes_string

col <- "b"

ggplot(data) + geom_point(aes_string(x="a", y=col))

messages.author: 68b661fcb57b94a9
messages.subject: labelling summary values
parts:
Was having trouble labelling the mean that's calculated using stat_summary. Taking initial example (now with group added; thanks Kohske),

tst.data <- data.frame (x = c(rep("Blue",500), rep("Red",500)), y=c(rnorm(500,3,6), rnorm(500,8,4) ) )
ggplot ( data = tst.data,aes(x,y)) + geom_point(alpha = .3) +
stat_summary(aes(group=1),fun.y = "mean",geom = "line")

Above works.

tst.data <- data.frame (x = c(rep("Blue",500), rep("Red",500)), y=c(rnorm(500,3,6), rnorm(500,8,4) ) )
ggplot ( data = tst.data,aes(x,y)) + geom_point(alpha = .3) +
stat_summary(aes(group=1),fun.y = "mean",geom = "line") +
stat_summary(aes(group=1),fun.y = "mean",geom = "text")

This doesn't. It asks for the label, but I'm not sure how to add it (adding it as I would a usual aesthetic doesn't work). And of course, once I add it, I'd like to be able to format it somehow (e.g. dollar).

Thanks again.



Adam Loveland

messages.subject: Re: labelling summary values
parts:
Adam_Loveland-QlCk...@public.gmane.org wrote:
> Was having trouble labelling the mean that's calculated using
> stat_summary. Taking initial example (now with group added; thanks
> Kohske),
>
> tst.data<- data.frame (x = c(rep("Blue",500), rep("Red",500)),
> y=c(rnorm(500,3,6), rnorm(500,8,4) ) )
> ggplot ( data = tst.data,aes(x,y)) + geom_point(alpha = .3) +
> stat_summary(aes(group=1),fun.y = "mean",geom = "line")
>
> Above works.
>
> tst.data<- data.frame (x = c(rep("Blue",500), rep("Red",500)),
> y=c(rnorm(500,3,6), rnorm(500,8,4) ) )
> ggplot ( data = tst.data,aes(x,y)) + geom_point(alpha = .3) +
> stat_summary(aes(group=1),fun.y = "mean",geom = "line") +
> stat_summary(aes(group=1),fun.y = "mean",geom = "text")
>
> This doesn't. It asks for the label, but I'm not sure how to add it
> (adding it as I would a usual aesthetic doesn't work). And of course, once
> I add it, I'd like to be able to format it somehow (e.g. dollar).
You have to specify it as the returned value from the summary.

stat_summary(aes(group=1, label=ggplot2::dollar(..y..)), fun.y = "mean",
geom = "text")

I don't know why you have to have ggplot2::dollar rather than just
dollar, though.
